correctness.rationale: Tabachnikov’s Lemma 7.1 for convex bicycle polygons, read in the original 2004 full preprint and page image, gives an isosceles trapezoid for each index i with bases ViVi+m and Vi+1Vi+m−1. Pair the trapezoids indexed i and i+m along their common long diagonal. Reflection of leg directions forces θ_i+θ_{i+m−1}≡θ_{i+m}+θ_{i−1} mod 2π, so strict exterior turning angles α_i and α_{i+m} agree (both in (0,π)). Total turn 2π gives a half-turn π per m edges and e_{i+m}=−e_i, hence Vi+m+Vi is constant. Center at zero; then Xi+m−1=−Xi−1, so equal side s and (m−1)-diagonal d yield s²+d²=2(||Xi||²+||Xi−1||²). Subtraction forces squared-radius period two. For odd m, the antipodal index shift swaps parity and equalizes all radii. Strict convexity gives consecutive central angle in (0,π), where equal chord length forces equal angle, hence regularity. For even m, original Theorem 10 gives nonregular one-parameter convex examples n even and k odd, with strict convex parameter choices. No finite experiment is invoked as an infinite proof.
risks: Strict convexity is used both to exclude the parallelogram branch and to identify turning/central angles; degenerate polygons excluded.

Connelly–Csikós examines local first-order flexibility, not global convex rigidity; Tabachnikov–Tsukerman 2012 Theorem 9 concerns the different line (4k,k). value.rationale: The original bicycle classification asks exactly which arithmetic (n,k) parameter families permit nonregular convex polygons. The nearest-to-half diagonal k=n/2−1 is a natural infinitely varying line, and the theorem supplies a global central-symmetry/two-radius mechanism and complete parity threshold: infinitely many new odd-m rigid cases with an already-known flexible complementary half. It is not arbitrary low-order enumeration or mere title/parameter renaming.

final_claim: Every strictly convex equilateral 2m-gon (m≥3) with equal (m−1)-neighbor diagonals is centrally symmetric and has squared vertex radii periodic with index shift two; for odd m this forces regularity, whereas for even m Tabachnikov’s existing even-n odd-k construction yields nonregular strictly convex examples.
limitations: Strict convexity essential; no classification of every nonregular even-m polygon.
Even-m flexibility existence is prior work, not claimed original.
